description: Lift and drag coefficients for the NACA 0012 airfoil as a function of angle of attack, at Re_c = 1e6, M = 0.15 (effectively incompressible). Generated with XFOIL v6.99 default panel discretization (200 panels), Mach correction enabled. XFOIL is a viscous panel/boundary-layer code that is accurate for attached subsonic flow up to roughly the stall angle; beyond that point the values here are unreliable and a RANS simulation will diverge from them.

convention.mach_number: Free-stream Mach. At M=0.15 compressibility is negligible.
convention.angle_of_attack: alpha in degrees, between the free-stream and the chord line
convention.Cl_Cd: Standard coefficients: Cl = lift / (0.5 * rho * U_inf^2 * c), Cd = drag / (0.5 * rho * U_inf^2 * c), for a chord-spanning 2-D section.

conditions.transition: free (XFOIL default; no fixed transition trip)

tolerance.rationale: A 2-D RANS at moderate Re typically matches XFOIL Cl within 5-10% in the linear regime (alpha < ~10 deg). Cd is much more mesh-sensitive — XFOIL's Cd reflects laminar-turbulent transition modelled via e^n; a fully-turbulent k-omega-SST RANS will over-predict Cd by 20-40%. The 30% Cd tolerance accommodates this; tighten if a transition model is enabled in OpenFOAM.

primary_citation: Drela, M. (1989). XFOIL: An analysis and design system for low Reynolds number airfoils. In Lecture Notes in Engineering, 54, Springer.
data_provenance: Generated with XFOIL v6.99 default settings on 2026-05-18. NACA 0012 at Re=1e6, M=0.15, alpha = 0..15 deg in 2-deg steps. Values are XFOIL's converged solution after default Ncrit=9 and full viscous-inviscid coupling. The polar can be regenerated by running XFOIL with the included input commands; see cases/examples/naca-0012/reference/README.md.
units: All non-dimensional. alpha in degrees, Cl and Cd are dimensionless.
